notice: Original personal-use review material. Educator review and learner validation are pending. Examples support self-review; this screen does not score your work or certify a level.
rights: Original SpeechCoachAI wording, 2026-10-25. Existing reference audio is unchanged; no publisher text, descriptor wording or learner response is copied.
selfReview: Did I communicate my chosen name, role and one interest?
Did I answer the related question rather than only ask one?
Was my wording meaningful, even if it differed from the example?
Did I use a model, frame, hints or corrective help? Keep that assistance visible.
Which one thing would I keep, and which one thing would I practise next?
Text work does not establish intelligibility; declined or missing audio stays not assessed.
independentCriterion: Draft local criterion: task success 2, vocabulary 2, grammar at least 1 and intelligibility at least 1, with all dimensions assessable and no in-task hints, models or corrections. These adopted pilot thresholds require qualified prospective review; no automatic score is produced.

dimensions.title: Task success
dimensions.notAssessed: The task was not attempted, key response evidence was deleted, or a different task/support condition was used.
anchors: 0 — The reviewer cannot identify the requested introduction meanings; for example, an unrelated message gives no chosen name, role or interest.
1 — Some requested information is understandable, but a fact or the related answer is missing; for example, a name and role without an interest or follow-up answer.
2 — A chosen name, role and interest plus a relevant follow-up answer are communicated. Fictional facts are allowed; elaborate wording is unnecessary.

dimensions.title: Vocabulary retrieval and use
dimensions.notAssessed: There is no suitable language sample or the target meaning was supplied by a model; exact phrase recall and communicative paraphrase must be reported separately.
anchors: 0 — Needed meanings cannot be recovered from the chosen words, even when the intended topic is known.
1 — Some intended meanings are communicated, with a missing or inaccurate choice that requires help or clarification.
2 — Words or natural paraphrases communicate the required meanings. For example, I enjoy walking conveys an interest without proving recall of I like.

dimensions.title: Grammar in available opportunities
dimensions.notAssessed: The response avoids a target or has no required opportunity. First-person introductions cannot establish third-person agreement.
anchors: 0 — Target forms usually prevent recovery of the intended meaning; the reviewer records which opportunity and meaning were lost.
1 — Target errors occur but meaning remains recoverable; for example, My name Noor and I study art may communicate a name and role despite a missing be form.
2 — Target forms are generally controlled where used; for example, My name is Noor. I study art. I like walking. Judge valid varieties and meaning, not grammar terminology.

dimensions.title: Intelligibility from actual audio
dimensions.notAssessed: No usable consented audio or qualified listening evidence is available. Text, transcript correctness and self-review cannot score this dimension.
anchors: 0 — An actual listener cannot recover most intended meaning from the audio; the reviewer records the affected words and listening conditions.
1 — An actual listener recovers the meaning with some effort or repetition. The observation must cite the recording and listening conditions.
2 — An actual listener readily understands the message. A retained accent is acceptable; speed or native-accent imitation is not the goal.

activities.explanation: The passage names English as the subject of study. A full sentence is optional for this comprehension question.
activities.boundary: An interest such as cooking does not answer what Mina studies.

activities.explanation: Use the name in the written source; a short answer is sufficient.
activities.boundary: Do not substitute the name heard in the different listening source.

activities.explanation: Likes and enjoys communicate the same interest here.
activities.boundary: The source does not say Mina is a cook; an interest is not a job.

activities.explanation: The audio says the speaker's name is Alex; no gender label is required.
activities.boundary: Reading Mina’s passage cannot establish this listening answer.

activities.explanation: The audio identifies a cook; it does not say Alex studies English.
activities.boundary: Do not infer listening comprehension from a transcript-only or quiet attempt.

activities.explanation: The audio names music as the interest.
activities.boundary: Mina’s cooking interest belongs to the reading, not this recording.

activities.explanation: I takes am in this statement: I am a student.
activities.boundary: Is and are do not agree with I. I'm a student is a natural full-message contraction, but the one-word gap asks for am.

activities.explanation: She takes is in this statement: She is a teacher.
activities.boundary: Am belongs with I; are belongs with you/we/they. A teacher describes she after be; it is a subject complement, not a direct object.

activities.explanation: With I, use the base form study in a simple-present statement.
activities.boundary: Studies agrees with he/she; studying alone needs another verb and does not fill this gap.

activities.explanation: With he, add -s: He works in a shop.
activities.boundary: Work is the I/you/we/they form here. A statement about yourself does not test he/she agreement; use the separate colleague task.

activities.explanation: Use do with you and the base verb like: Do you like music?
activities.boundary: Does takes he/she plus a base verb. Are you like music? does not ask the intended question.

activities.explanation: Different introductions can communicate a chosen name. Fictional names are welcome.
activities.boundary: I am Noor can be communicatively valid without demonstrating recall of the specific phrase My name is.

activities.explanation: From introduces the place of origin. The place may be fictional.
activities.boundary: I live in Cebu gives a current home; it does not necessarily state where someone comes from.

activities.explanation: Both can answer this practice cue about study or work.
activities.boundary: A work response can succeed communicatively without demonstrating retrieval of the selected study sense.

activities.explanation: Accept meaningful expressions of an interest; the phrase I like is one useful option.
activities.boundary: Enjoy walking is a valid message but is not evidence that the exact target I like was recalled.
Nice to see you again assumes an earlier meeting and may not suit this cue.

alternatives: Hello. My name is Noor. I study art. I like walking. In my free time, I walk in the park.
activities.explanation: Check for a chosen name, a role, an interest and an answer to one related question. Fiction is allowed.
activities.boundary: Saving or self-review is participation, not independent task success. A script-supported retry stays assisted.

alternatives: I included a name, a role and an interest, and answered the follow-up. I want to practise one verb next.
activities.explanation: Review what your attempt actually contains and choose one next action; identifying a gap is useful.
activities.boundary: Do not convert self-confidence, completion or an example match into a verified English-level score.

alternatives: My name is Noor. I study art. I like walking. In my free time, I walk in the park.
activities.explanation: Write the same three meanings as the spoken route and answer its related follow-up.
activities.boundary: Asking a question instead of answering one does not meet the follow-up meaning. Written practice supplies no intelligibility or speaking assessment.

method: Notice word jobs and sentence parts
priorities: Separate word class from sentence function. A noun can appear in the predicate.
Distinguish a subject complement after be from an object after an action verb.
Practise subject–verb matching in context. Missing third-person opportunities are not errors.
packs.criteria: Record five concept responses separately from five productive forms and the colleague application. A terminology answer cannot establish communication or grammar retention.
packs.boundary: Personal practice only. The foundation pack does not add required course activities or an automatic mastery gate.

priorities: First check whether name, role, interest and a related answer are understandable.
Then focus on one high-impact target form. Keep a valid answer; do not invent errors.
packs.criteria: For a reviewed future check, keep the five fresh target responses separate from the linked independent communicative task. The adopted 4/5 criterion requires prospective review and actual unaided responses.
packs.boundary: Reduced support after seeing a model is practice, not a fresh independent baseline. Current open responses are not automatically scored.

method: Use the pattern in a new colleague message
priorities: Explain subject–verb agreement or do/does plus a base verb when that target is actually used.
Preserve the intended meaning and accept natural alternatives. Avoid correcting every unrelated detail.
packs.criteria: Keep five fresh productive responses separate from two natural third-person opportunities in the colleague message. A target not elicited is not assessed. The adopted 4/5 check is not a verified score here.
packs.boundary: Selecting a choice or knowing a label does not prove productive use; a first-person response alone cannot prove he/she agreement.

priorities: Check whether the questions relate to this source and the follow-up uses the supplied answer.
Keep all three source points without adding a job or other unstated fact. Prioritize fidelity before style.
packs.criteria: Mina is the name, English is the subject of study, and cooking is the interest. Check two relevant questions including a response-dependent follow-up, then a faithful three-point summary. These are specialty criteria, not INTRO-01 baseline scores.
packs.boundary: This pack uses a written source and gives reading-based practice only. Calling Mina a cook invents a job. Do not infer listening skill, accent or speaking fluency.
